fatal_errors: The hypothesis replaces the target AlCoCrFeNi coating and 550 °C annealing intervention with passivation treatments on nominally bare stainless steel.
Radiation-induced degradation and combined chemical-radiation protection are central claims but are not supported by the cited evidence.
The experiment co-varies passive-film thickness and chromium enrichment, so it cannot determine which property governs any observed protection.
explanation: This is a scientifically plausible generic stainless-steel passivation hypothesis, but it is not a reconstruction of the target study. It misses the APS-deposited AlCoCrFeNi coating, the annealing-temperature series and 550 °C optimum, grain refinement and BCC/FCC structure, Al-rich protection, hardness changes, and cyclic molten-salt corrosion at 900 °C. Its prediction of lower Icorr and more noble Ecorr from a Cr-rich passive layer partially agrees with one component of the target mechanism. E1 and E2 support chromium as a dominant passivation former in CoCrFeMnNi alloys under NaCl and sulfuric-acid testing, but they do not validate radiation effects, film-thickness dependence, or direct applicability to pre-passivated 304 stainless steel. The untreated and intentionally degraded controls and explicit falsification rule are useful, although independent manipulation of film composition and thickness, replication, and specified radiation dose and exposure duration would be needed for strong causal discrimination.
